items.reason: Valid: DefaultRequest.bodyStream(long) (DefaultRequest.java:276-279) re-implements the 1..JsonBodyReader.MAX_LIMIT check that DefaultRestApp.byteLimit (DefaultRestApp.java:300-305) already owns as 'the range of every body limit'. byteLimit("maxBytes", x) produces the identical message "maxBytes must be in 1..1073741824 bytes: x" and the same IllegalArgumentException, so delegating is behaviour-preserving. Both files are in the write set; byteLimit is a private static helper, so widening it to package-private changes no public signature.
items.fix_hint: In DefaultRestApp change `private static long byteLimit(String name, long bytes)` to package-private `static long byteLimit(...)`. In DefaultRequest.bodyStream(long) replace the if/throw block with `return rawStream(DefaultRestApp.byteLimit("maxBytes", maxBytes));` and keep the javadoc. No test changes.

items.reason: Already single-sourced: all three fields reference the one constant JsonBodyReader.DEFAULT_LIMIT, so they cannot drift. This is the same pattern jsonLimit uses (DefaultRestApp.java:113, Dispatcher.java:98, DefaultRequest.java:91), and the Dispatcher/DefaultRequest values are only pre-freeze fallbacks that the setters overwrite. Renaming or relocating the 'JSON-named' constant would mean editing JsonBodyReader.java, which is outside the write set.

This follows the existing convention: proxyTrust reaches Dispatcher and DefaultRequest through the same post-construction setters (Dispatcher.java:214, DefaultRequest.java:682), which DefaultRestApp.freeze calls at DefaultRestApp.java:1349-1350. Wiring it through the constructors would mean adding a parameter to the public Dispatcher/DefaultRequest constructors (a public signature change) or adding yet another constructor overload. Either is out of bounds for a behaviour-preserving clean-code fix.

The two delegates wrap different input types (RecordingInput vs CountingInput). Sharing them needs a new generic helper file (new files are forbidden) or makes one test class depend on another's nested class. Each test class keeping its own HttpExchange delegate is the established test convention (see ResponseOnAbortTest, HttpAdapterSpiTest, internal/LifecycleExchange).

Not a real defect. The overrides are intentional defensive code: RawBodyStream's consumed/closed tracking relies on a reset never handing bytes back, and its comment says so independently of the source. Without the overrides, FilterInputStream would forward mark/reset to whatever source it wraps, so RawBodyStream's own contract would quietly depend on LimitedInputStream's implementation. Removing three trivial methods would weaken a local invariant to remove a negligible duplication.
